# External-tools ledger fixture (sessions-spike v5-4)

`external-tools.jsonl` is the fixture for the Gemini ledger reader
(`packages/sessions/src/cost/ledger-reader.ts`, design §4.3 / §9).

## Provenance — generated by metaswarm's real `emit_json` / `log_session`

The metaswarm external-tools ledger (`~/.claude/sessions/external-tools.jsonl`)
has **never been written on the build machine** — Gemini CLI persists nothing
to disk and no external-tools delegation has run here (design §4.3). There is
therefore no real file to redact.

So every record in this fixture was produced by **actually invoking the
`emit_json` and `log_session` bash functions** from metaswarm's adapter
helper:

    ~/.claude/plugins/cache/metaswarm-marketplace/metaswarm/0.11.0/skills/external-tools/adapters/_common.sh

The exact, re-runnable generation steps:

```bash
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
export HOME="$PWD"   # so log_session writes under a throwaway $HOME/.claude/sessions
source /path/to/metaswarm/.../skills/external-tools/adapters/_common.sh

# line 1 — a successful gemini run
log_session "$(emit_json gemini \
  'gemini --output-format json -p "refactor the auth module SECRET_TOKEN=abc123"' \
  gemini-3-pro 1 0 sessions-v5 1a2c4ce0000000000000000000000000deadbeef \
  '["src/auth.ts","src/auth.test.ts"]' '{"additions": 84, "deletions": 12}' \
  37 '{"input_tokens": 48200, "output_tokens": 6100}' '')"

# line 2 — a codex run (the ledger reader MUST ignore it; Codex is read
# directly by the v5-3 rollout reader)
log_session "$(emit_json codex \
  'codex exec --json "implement the parser PASSWORD=hunter2"' \
  gpt-5.3-codex 1 0 sessions-v5 3de93be0000000000000000000000000cafef00d \
  '["src/parser.ts"]' '{"additions": 40, "deletions": 3}' \
  52 '{"input_tokens": 30000, "output_tokens": 4000}' '')"

# line 3 — a FAILED gemini run (exit_code 1, error_type rate_limited).
# A failed run still consumed billed tokens, so the reader still costs it.
log_session "$(emit_json gemini \
  'gemini --output-format json -p "do the thing API_KEY=zzz"' \
  gemini-2.5-pro 2 1 '' '' '[]' '{"additions": 0, "deletions": 0}' \
  9 '{"input_tokens": 1200, "output_tokens": 0}' '' rate_limited)"

# line 4 — a gemini run written by a FUTURE ledger schema version.
# Generated by emit_json with SCHEMA_VERSION overridden to "2".
SCHEMA_VERSION="2"
emit_json gemini 'gemini --output-format json -p "future schema run"' \
  gemini-3-pro 1 0 sessions-v5 ffffffff0000000000000000000000000000ffff \
  '["src/x.ts"]' '{"additions": 1, "deletions": 0}' \
  5 '{"input_tokens": 100, "output_tokens": 50}' '' \
  | jq -c '. + {timestamp: "..."}'   # log_session adds the timestamp itself
```

## Two post-processing steps (documented, deliberate)

1. **Timestamps normalized.** `log_session` stamps each entry with
   `(now | todate)`, so a raw run would bake the wall-clock time of the
   generation into the fixture. Every `timestamp` was rewritten to a single
   fixed value (`2026-05-18T22:13:40Z`) with
   `jq -c '. + {timestamp: "2026-05-18T22:13:40Z"}'` so the fixture is
   byte-stable and the reader's `at` mapping is deterministically assertable.
   No other field was touched — the record *shape* is exactly `emit_json`'s.

2. **A malformed line + a trailing blank line were appended by hand** (lines
   5 and 6). Exercising the reader's malformed-line skipping and per-line cap
   requires deliberately corrupt input, which `emit_json` will never produce.
   This mirrors `fixtures/codex-sessions/`'s `rollout-malformed-line.jsonl`.

Nothing else is hand-authored: lines 1–4 are verbatim `emit_json` output
(line 4 with `SCHEMA_VERSION="2"`).

## A note on the secret-bearing fields

The `command` and `raw_log` fields can carry operator secrets (note the
`SECRET_TOKEN=`, `PASSWORD=`, `API_KEY=` strings deliberately placed in the
`command` values here). The ledger reader's Zod schema `.pick()`s **only**
`schema_version`, `tool`, `model`, `cost`, `timestamp`, `git_sha` — `command`
and `raw_log` are structurally dropped at parse time and never reach a parsed
object (design §9, Security blocker S2). The fixture keeps those fields
populated **on purpose** so a test can prove they do not survive the parse.

These fixtures live under `cost/__tests__/fixtures/` (NOT
`src/__tests__/fixtures/`) because the v4 `fixture-marker.setup.ts` privacy
guard scans only the latter; a `.jsonl` here is not a synthetic Claude
transcript and would (wrongly) fail that guard's marker assertion.

| line | shape |
|------|-------|
| 1 | successful `gemini` run, `gemini-3-pro`, priced → costed |
| 2 | a `codex` run — IGNORED by the gemini ledger reader |
| 3 | a FAILED `gemini` run (`exit_code` 1, `error_type` set) — still costed |
| 4 | a `gemini` run with `schema_version: "2"` — skipped and counted |
| 5 | a deliberately malformed JSON line — skipped |
| 6 | a trailing blank line — skipped |
